facts.text: Vinemont was renamed in 1898 when Chicago businessmen founded Alabama Vineyard and Winery Company, planting European grapes on its fertile hillsides.
The town sits at about 1,100 feet, one of Alabama's highest elevations, giving it a cool mountain air that attracted early settlers and later resort visitors.
Vinemont’s post office opened in 1887 and the community became a whistle stop on the Louisville & Nashville Railroad, originally called Holmes Gap.
The Battleground School in South Vinemont is listed on the Alabama Register of Landmarks and Heritage, highlighting the town’s historic education legacy.
The area that became Vinemont was opened to settlement after the 1830s treaties that removed Cherokee, Chickasaw, and Creek tribes, marking the start of farming in the region.
